firms.name: 8VC
firms.overview: Founded in 2015 by Palantir/Addepar co-founder Joe Lonsdale (originally 'Formation 8' lineage), with co-founders Jake Medwell and others; HQ moved to Austin. Invests 'at every stage' across defense/gov, AI and enterprise software, healthcare/bio, logistics and industrial tech, and incubates companies via 8VC Build. Closed 8VC Fund VII at US$1.5bn in Jul-2026 (largest to date), taking committed capital to >US$6bn. Portfolio anchors include Palantir, Anduril, Oculus, Flexport, Guardant Health, Oscar, Saronic, Epirus, Vercel and Cognition.

key_people.name: Joe Lonsdale
key_people.title: Founder & Managing Partner
key_people.focus: Defense, gov tech, fintech, AI; Palantir co-founder

firms.team_size: ~49 listed on website; ~20 on investment team
firms.performance: Fund-level returns not publicly disclosed in sources reviewed. Track record anchored by Lonsdale-network outcomes (Palantir, Oculus->Meta 2014, Anduril, Guardant Health IPO, OpenGov sale ~US$1.8bn, Deliverr->Shopify US$2.1bn, Casetext->Thomson Reuters US$650m). Some exposure to underperformers (Wish, Blend).
firms.recent_activity: 2025-26: led/co-led Cognition (Mar-2025, ~US$4bn), Epirus Series D, Bedrock Robotics launch; Q3-Q4 2026 activity includes Armadin Series B, BigHat Biosciences Series C, Luminary Series A. Thematic tilt to 'AI industrial revolution' - defense, robotics, logistics, healthcare AI.
firms.watch_items: Key-person/brand concentration around Joe Lonsdale, whose political profile is high; reputational scrutiny of team members with links to sanctioned-country oligarch families (press-reported). Defense concentration (Anduril, Saronic, Epirus) adds policy/procurement correlation.

firms.name: Accel
firms.overview: Founded 1983 by Arthur Patterson and Jim Swartz, Accel runs early-stage funds in the US, Europe/Israel and India plus the global Leaders growth programme. Defining early bets include Facebook, Atlassian, Slack, Flipkart, CrowdStrike and Spotify. In 2026 it raised ~$8.5bn: $5bn for late stage (Leaders V $4bn + $650m sidecar, April) and $3.5bn across four early-stage funds (August), including a new $1.35bn global expansion fund. Accel-KKR is a separate software-focused PE firm (joint venture origins) and is not covered here.
firms.performance: Fund-level returns not verified this pass. India VIII reportedly >55% undeployed when IX closed (Aug 2026). Defining multiples historically from Facebook, Flipkart, Atlassian, Slack.
firms.recent_activity: Co-led Cursor Series D, led Lovable Series A and co-led its $13.3bn round, led Supabase D/E, Vercel E/F; early cheques into Thinking Machines and Periodic Labs; growing Europe/Israel AI programme.
firms.watch_items: Partner transition (Daniel Levine stepping back from new funds); India deployment pace slowed; large Leaders vehicle raises entry-price risk in AI growth rounds.

firms.name: AlleyCorp
firms.overview: Founded in 2007 by Kevin Ryan (ex-DoubleClick CEO; co-founder of MongoDB, Business Insider, Gilt, Zola) as a family office that incubated companies. It took external capital for the first time with a US$250m fund in 2024, then raised a US$335m second fund in Jul-2026. It invests early (first checks under US$10m) across healthcare, deep tech and general tech, and still incubates (Pearl Health, Chamber Cardio, Transcend Therapeutics). Legacy holdings sit in AlleyCorp Enterprises, the former family office; per the website disclaimer they are not investments of the registered adviser (AlleyCorp Advisers).
firms.check_size: Pre-seed to Series A, first checks <US$10m
firms.performance: No audited fund returns disclosed; Fortune (Jul-2026) cites an anonymous source claiming an all-time ~60% IRR on prior (largely family-office) investments - unverified (ESTIMATE). Realised highlights: MongoDB IPO (2017), Business Insider (Axel Springer, 2015), Transcend Therapeutics (Otsuka, 2026, up to US$1.225bn). Portfolio counts eight unicorns incl. Rogo, ShopMy, Valar Atomics, Thyme Care.
firms.recent_activity: 2025-26 activity: led Clarasight Series A, Birches Health Series A, PraxisPro seed and Appetronix seed; participated in Portal Space Systems Series A and avoMD; added Alexi Nazem as GP for healthcare. Ryan has floated a future US$500-600m fund (biotech practice / geography).
firms.watch_items: Very short institutional track record (first external fund 2024); historical returns sit mostly in a family-office entity legally separate from the adviser. Key-person risk on Kevin Ryan.

firms.name: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)
firms.overview: Founded in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz. a16z is a multi-strategy venture platform built around vertical practices: AI infra and apps, growth, crypto, American Dynamism (defense/gov/industrial), bio + health, fintech, consumer and games. Its differentiators are a large platform and marketing operation, crypto and policy capabilities in Washington, D.C., and a growth fund big enough to lead late-stage AI rounds. In January 2026 it closed just over $15bn across five strategies and said this was more than 18% of US venture dollars allocated in 2025; reported AUM exceeds $90bn. It opened a Seoul office for crypto in Dec 2025.
firms.check_size: Seed $0.5-5m; A/B $10-75m; growth $50m-$1bn+ (e.g. led Thinking Machines ~$2bn seed)
firms.team_size: >500 employees (2024); 'many hundreds' across 5 US offices plus Seoul (2026)
firms.performance: a16z does not publish fund-level DPI. Newcomer reported (2024) that it has returned at least $25bn net to LPs since 2009, and that Fund III (2012, $0.9bn) was held at 9.4x net TVPI. Its Coinbase stake (2013 entry, ~$25m) was estimated at ~$9.7bn at the 2021 direct listing. Washington State Investment Board's Q3-2025 report has no a16z rows, and no CalPERS or UTIMCO a16z fund-level figures were found in this pass. Known losses include the Twitter take-private (~$288m loss reported by Sep 2024), BuzzFeed and parts of the 2021-22 crypto vintage.
firms.recent_activity: 2025-26 activity is centred on AI. a16z led Thinking Machines Lab's ~$2bn seed (Jul 2025), co-led Anduril's 2026 round (~$61bn) with Thrive, and backs Mistral, ElevenLabs, SSI, Cursor, Harvey and Abridge. The American Dynamism practice (Shield AI, Saronic, Castelion, Hadrian, Applied Intuition) and crypto both kept heavy deal flow.
firms.watch_items: Scale and concentration: the firm reports >18% of 2025 US VC dollars, so marks depend on a handful of AI mega-rounds. LPs should watch DPI on the 2021-22 vintages, especially crypto. Partners' political and policy roles bring reputational and key-person exposure.

firms.name: Atomico
firms.overview: Skype co-founder Niklas Zennström founded Atomico in 2006. It is Europe's best-known Series A-to-pre-IPO tech investor. It has made 155+ investments across 15 countries, and about one in six portfolio companies has been valued above $1B. In Sep 2024 it closed its largest raise, $1.24B: Venture VI ($485M, below its $600M target) and Growth VI ($754M, above target). Klarna's 2025 NYSE IPO and Lime's 2026 Nasdaq listing are the latest liquidity. It also publishes the annual State of European Tech report.
firms.performance: Fund-level IRR/TVPI not publicly disclosed in sources reviewed. Defining realisations: Supercell (Tencent, 2016), Klarna (NYSE IPO Sep 2025), Wolt (DoorDash, 2022), Peakon (Workday, 2021), Hinge Health (NYSE 2025), Lime (Nasdaq 2026). The Venture VI target shortfall points to some LP selectivity.
firms.recent_activity: In Jul 2026 it joined Neko Health's ~$700M Series C alongside Lightspeed and General Catalyst. It was a finalist (with EQT) for the EU's €5B Scaleup Europe Fund, which EQT won. Partner Irina Haivas departed. Growth VI positions include DeepL, Corti and Pelago.
firms.watch_items: Partner turnover, and losing the EU Scaleup mandate to EQT. Venture VI undershot its target. Long hold periods for European growth with thin IPO markets.

firms.name: Bain Capital Ventures
firms.overview: Bain Capital Ventures is the venture arm of Bain Capital (~$225bn platform), investing seed to growth in AI applications and infrastructure, fintech, security, commerce and, increasingly, physical AI and science. It has launched 400+ companies, with 173 exits and 16 IPOs (Feb 2024). It closed Fund XI at $1.6bn (Sep 2026, above target), pitched as early-stage capital for a 'post-AGI' world, after Fund X ($1.44bn) and Select IV ($0.48bn) in 2023. Recent defining outcomes are Moveworks (ServiceNow) and MaintainX (Autodesk agreement, $3.6bn).
firms.team_size: 74 total (23 investing, 29 platform, 22 operating) as of Feb 2024
firms.performance: Fund-level returns not publicly disclosed in sources reviewed. Firm reports 173 exits and 16 IPOs (Feb 2024); notable realizations include DocuSign, Twilio, LinkedIn, Flywire, AvidXchange, Moveworks (ServiceNow) and MaintainX (Autodesk, $3.6bn agreed).
firms.recent_activity: Heavy AI deployment: Etched ($700m at $21bn), Norm Ai ($120m Series C at $1.2bn), Feathery Series A, plus Cognition, Decagon, Legora, Poolside, Crusoe, Periodic Labs, Chai Discovery and Sunday Robotics.
firms.watch_items: Increasing concentration in high-priced AI rounds; Bain Capital platform affiliation can create perceived conflicts/sourcing benefits. Fund returns opaque to non-LPs.

firms.name: Balderton Capital
firms.overview: Founded in 2000 as Benchmark Capital Europe, Balderton became independent in 2007 and is one of Europe's largest early-stage investors. It has backed ~300 European-founded companies and runs separate early-stage and growth funds; it has raised $5.7B cumulatively. In Aug 2024 it raised $1.3B across Early Stage Fund IX ($615M) and Growth Fund II ($685M), ~80% from existing LPs. Revolut is the firm-defining asset: Balderton led the 2015 seed (£1M) and realised ~$2B in the 2025 secondary, and Dealroom estimates Revolut at ~78% of its holdings value.
firms.performance: Fund-level net IRR not publicly disclosed. Fund V (~$305M) returned more than 25x per FT sources, largely from Revolut; the Revolut seed check is ~2,000x on paper. ~$2B was realised in the Revolut secondary in H2 2025. Other exits: Dream Games (CVC, 2025), GoCardless (Mollie, 2025), Contentful (Salesforce, announced Jun 2026), Darktrace, Depop.
firms.recent_activity: In 2026 it led Stream's $90M Series D (Jan), Geordie's $30M A and Grand Games' $70M B (May), and invested in Taktile (Jun). It promoted three MDs (Jul 2026) and launched the 'Built in Europe' campaign.
firms.watch_items: Extreme NAV concentration in Revolut (~78% of estimated holdings). Partial DPI has been realised, but remaining returns hinge on the Revolut IPO timing (CEO says 2+ years away). It largely missed the foundation-model wave.

firms.name: Battery Ventures
firms.overview: Battery Ventures is a global, technology-focused firm investing from seed through growth and majority/buyout ("majority growth") in application software, infrastructure software, and industrial tech and life-science tools. Since inception (ex-seed) it has backed 530+ companies, with 73 IPOs and 225+ M&A events through Sep 2025. It closed Battery Ventures XV at $3.25bn in a single, oversubscribed close in February 2026 and says it has returned $10bn+ to LPs over the past five years. Its hybrid venture/control-buyout model sets it apart from pure VCs.
firms.check_size: Early $5-20m; growth $20-150m; majority growth/buyout up to several hundred million (ESTIMATE)
firms.team_size: ~10 GPs, 31 partners total; 45+ investment professionals across six offices
firms.performance: No fund-level net IRR/TVPI located in public-pension disclosures this session (Nevada PERS and Hawaii ERS have historically reported Battery funds; Hawaii flagged three 2007-10 Battery funds as top performers, figures paywalled). Firm discloses $10bn+ returned over the past five years, 15 exit events in 2025, 73 IPOs and 225+ M&A events since inception.
firms.recent_activity: 2025-26 activity spans AI apps (1mind), AI security (Imper.ai, Koi Security), vertical SaaS (Vetspire, Mews) and industrial majority deals (Phigenics). XV (Feb 2026) is focused on AI-enabled software and infrastructure.
firms.watch_items: Blend of venture and control buyouts complicates benchmarking; total regulatory AUM not verified (AUM figure is an estimate of cumulative capital). Portfolio attribution here partly from aggregators where battery.com could not be fetched.

firms.name: Benchmark
firms.overview: Founded 1995 with an equal-partnership model (no senior/junior partners, equal economics), Benchmark typically leads first institutional rounds and takes board seats. Historic hits include eBay, Uber, Twitter, Instagram, Snap and Zillow; the Cerebras IPO (May 2026) returned ~$3.2bn on paper. In June 2026 it broke a ~20-year ~$425m fund-size discipline, raising $2bn: a $750m early-stage fund and its first-ever $1.25bn growth fund. Partnership has turned over: Everett Randle (ex-Kleiner) and Jack Altman joined; Sarah Tavel moved to venture partner; Victor Lazarte left.
firms.performance: Per Wikipedia (citing press): first eight funds (1995-2019) returned >7.5x net of fees and carry; the 2020 fund reportedly >10x; 2024 fund ~3x. Cerebras: ~$268m invested, ~$3.2bn at IPO price (~12x gross, unrealised). Pension LP disclosures not pulled this pass.
firms.recent_activity: AI-heavy early-stage leads (Sierra, Mercor, Legora, Fireworks, LangChain, Gumloop, HeyGen, 11x, Manus); first growth fund to concentrate into 5-6 large bets.
firms.watch_items: Style drift and key-person transition (new growth strategy, GP turnover); Manus deal drew regulatory/political scrutiny; very small team means concentrated judgement risk.

firms.name: Bessemer Venture Partners
firms.overview: Bessemer traces its roots to Bessemer Securities (Phipps family, Carnegie Steel fortune, 1911) and is one of the oldest US venture firms. It runs a flat partnership investing from seed to growth across cloud/enterprise software, fintech, healthcare, consumer and deep tech, with dedicated India and Israel programs and the BVP Forge growth-buyout strategy (launched 2022). Its 'State of the Cloud' research and Cloud 100 list are central to its cloud-software brand. In September 2026 it closed $5.75bn in a single close ($1.75bn seed/early, $4.0bn growth) across BVP XIII, Century Fund III and LP vehicles, tilting capital toward growth-stage AI.

firms.recent_activity: Active across AI apps and infra: led Upwind's $250m Series B at $1.5bn (Jan 2026) and Legora's Series C (2025); holds positions in Anthropic, Perplexity and Abridge. New $5.75bn (Sep 2026) is ~70% growth capital, signalling larger cheques into AI leaders.

firms.name: Coatue Management
firms.overview: Philippe Laffont founded Coatue in 1999 after working at Tiger Management. It is a technology crossover manager that runs public long/short funds alongside private Venture, Growth and Tactical (structured debt/equity) strategies. Thomas Laffont leads the private side. Coatue's site lists 250+ active private companies, featuring Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, SpaceX and Cursor. In 2025-26 it was one of the most active mega-round leads: it co-led Anthropic's Series G, co-led Anysphere's Series D, led Databricks' $5bn round at $190bn, and led CoreWeave's pre-IPO round. It launched the semi-liquid CTEK Innovation Fund for wealth channels in 2025. Bloomberg reported in March 2026 that Coatue was planning a long-biased crossover AI fund.

firms.performance: Coatue does not publish private fund performance. Public reporting is about the hedge fund (it avoided sharp losses in the April 2025 tariff sell-off) and the 2022 drawdown, when Coatue was among the crossover funds hit hardest by private-mark resets. We found no 2024-26 pension IRR/TVPI disclosure for the Growth funds in this pass. The Information has reported that Coatue came under pressure from its late-stage 2021 bets.
firms.recent_activity: Coatue led or co-led AI mega-rounds through 2025-26: CoreWeave ($1.1bn, 2024), Harvey Series E co-lead (2025), Anysphere Series D co-lead (Nov 2025), Anthropic Series G co-lead (Feb 2026) and Series H co-lead (May 2026), and Databricks $5bn lead (Aug 2026). It also started Next Frontier, a data-center land joint venture with Fluidstack (May 2026), and was reported as lead new investor in a Blue Origin round.
firms.watch_items: Mark-up risk: the portfolio is concentrated in AI names at peak valuations. Crossover public/private structures can move private marks with listed comps. The firm is increasingly pushing products into the wealth channel (CTEK on iCapital and CAIS).

firms.name: Conviction (Sarah Guo)
firms.overview: Sarah Guo founded Conviction in 2022 after leaving Greylock. It is an AI-native 'Software 3.0' seed/Series A firm. Fund I ($101M) was followed by Fund II ($230M, Jan 2025), when ex-Sequoia partner Mike Vernal joined as GP. A third fund has since been raised: press in Aug 2026 put the three funds at 'close to a billion dollars'. Conviction is small (~8 staff, 4 investors) but reportedly has backed 6 AI-native companies above $10B valuation, including Harvey, Cognition, Baseten and Sierra. It increasingly co-leads large follow-ons, for example co-leading Baseten's $1.5B round in 2026. Guo co-hosts the No Priors podcast with Elad Gil.
firms.check_size: Seed $1-5m; Series A/follow-on $5-25m; selective large co-leads
firms.performance: Not publicly disclosed. Fund I (2022 vintage) holds early positions in Harvey (first check pre-fund, personal), Baseten, Cognition, Sierra and Mistral, all with large 2025-26 mark-ups. These are unrealised; no DPI has been disclosed. Uplimit (acquired by Handshake, Jun 2026) is the only disclosed exit.
firms.recent_activity: In 2026 Conviction co-led Baseten's $1.5B round (Jun) and participated in Harvey's $550M round (Sep). New investments include Warp Sciences ($215M A, Oct 2026) and Keenable ($26M seed, Aug 2026). It has 108 tracked investments per CB Insights.
firms.watch_items: Extreme key-person concentration (Guo/Vernal) and a very young track record, all 2022+ vintages. Returns rest on a handful of AI marks at 20x+ revenue, with no DPI yet. Fund sizes are scaling fast (from $101M to ~$1B cumulative).

firms.name: DCVC (Data Collective)
firms.overview: DCVC was founded by Matt Ocko and Zachary Bogue as Data Collective. It backs deep-tech founders using computation and engineering in industrial, climate, space, defense, computing and bio markets. DCVC Bio runs a dedicated life-sciences franchise, and DCVC has added climate-specific capital. Its portfolio page lists ~290 companies, including IPOs (Rocket Lab, Planet, SentinelOne, Confluent, Elastic, Ginkgo, AbCellera, Recursion, Oklo, and Fervo in May 2026) and 60+ acquisitions such as Kaggle, Firebase, Blue River, Nervana and MosaicML. It closed $700m+ across funds in September 2024 and $1bn in July 2023.

firms.check_size: Seed/Series A $1-20m; selective growth follow-ons via opportunity funds (not disclosed)
firms.performance: Fund-level returns not found in sources reviewed. Rhode Island State Investment Commission publishes a DCVC Bio II LP report (data.treasury.ri.gov), not retrieved in this batch. The exit record is strong: 14 listed public names on DCVC's own page, including Rocket Lab, Planet, SentinelOne, Confluent (IBM agreed to acquire for ~$11bn, announced Dec 2025), Oklo and Fervo, plus 60+ M&A exits.
firms.recent_activity: 2025-26 activity centers on nuclear/fusion (Radiant, Pacific Fusion, Kairos), AI compute (Unconventional AI, SF Compute), quantum (Atom Computing, Mesa Quantum, Iceberg) and AI-bio. It led Proxima's $80m seed (Jan 2026) and joined humans& and Recursive Superintelligence.
firms.watch_items: Large exposure to listed small/mid-cap deep tech (Ginkgo, Desktop Metal, Evolv) has been volatile. Desktop Metal went bankrupt in 2025 after its sale to Nano Dimension. Exit timing and distributions depend heavily on public markets.

firms.name: Deerfield Management
firms.overview: Founded in 1994 by Arnold Snider (a Tiger Cub) and led since the 2000s by Managing Partner/CEO James Flynn. A healthcare-only investor across public equities, structured finance/royalties, private growth and venture, incubation (Deerfield Discovery & Development, 3DC) and research partnerships with 29 institutions (Harvard Lab1636, Broad, WashU). HQ is the Cure innovation campus at 345 Park Ave South. Its venture series is the Healthcare Innovations Funds (I $550m 2015; II $840m 2020; III >$600m 2025); a share of carry goes to the Deerfield Foundation.
firms.performance: No fund-level returns disclosed. Public hedge funds reported +11% in 2018 (press). 418 lifetime investments / ~130-140 exits / 3 unicorns per third-party trackers; ranked #10 biotech VC in the 2026 Strebulaev-Jackson ranking. Notable positions: BridgeBio, Nuvalent (co-founded), Bicara, Arvinas, Insulet; losses include Invitae (Ch.11, 2024).
firms.recent_activity: 2026: led Neomorph's US$100m Series B; joined Ray Therapeutics' US$125m Series B; launched Boulevard Bio (US$65m, 3DC incubation); Setara Biosciences US$90m Series A and Ascertain Series B (Oct-2026). Continued take-private/structured activity (Singular Genomics 2025).
firms.watch_items: 2017 insider-trading prosecution of two traders (convictions vacated 2022) and US$4.6m SEC settlement on controls - compliance history LPs will diligence. Blending of public/structured/private strategies creates cross-holding conflicts.

firms.name: Dragoneer Investment Group
firms.overview: Marc Stad (ex-TPG, McKinsey) founded Dragoneer in 2012. It is a growth investor that writes large, concentrated, long-duration checks across late-stage private and public technology, and it pioneered the 'IPO-crossover' model (Spotify, Airbnb, Uber, Snowflake, DoorDash). It ran three SPACs in 2020-21 (CCC Intelligent Solutions, Cvent). In 2025-26 it has been one of the largest AI-lab check writers: it led OpenAI's ~$8.3bn Aug 2025 tranche, co-led Anthropic's Series G, and was a lead on Anthropic's $65bn Series H. Fund VII closed at $4.3bn in Dec 2025, larger than Fund VI ($3.8bn, 2022). Dragoneer also runs a large evergreen vehicle and a ~$1bn continuation fund holding OpenAI/SpaceX.
firms.performance: Not publicly disclosed. We found no pension IRR/TVPI in this pass. SPAC outcomes were mixed: CCC traded near deal value, and Cvent was taken private by Blackstone at $8.50/sh, below the $10 SPAC price. Fund VII raising above Fund VI in a tough 2025 market suggests LP confidence.
firms.recent_activity: Led OpenAI's ~$8.3bn tranche (Aug 2025) and joined its Oct 2025 secondary at $500bn and Mar 2026 round at $852bn. Co-led Anthropic's Series G (Feb 2026) and Series H (May 2026). Led ClickHouse's $400m Series D (Jan 2026) and Helsing's ~€1bn+ round (May 2026, with Lightspeed).
firms.watch_items: Single-name concentration in OpenAI and Anthropic at very high valuations. The continuation-fund structure raises GP-led secondary governance questions. A small team relative to AUM increases key-person dependence on Stad.

firms.name: Eclipse (Eclipse Ventures)
firms.overview: Lior Susan founded Eclipse in 2015. It backs and incubates companies that rebuild physical industries (manufacturing, logistics, transportation, energy, compute and defense) with software, AI and advanced hardware. Defining positions are Cerebras (IPO May 2026), Redwood Materials (Eclipse led the 2025 Series E), Wayve and Tenstorrent, and in-house incubations such as Bright Machines and Mytra. In April 2026 Eclipse closed Fund VI ($720m) and Early Growth Fund III ($591m), $1.3bn combined, taking AUM to ~$10bn.
firms.performance: Fund-level returns not publicly disclosed. The Cerebras IPO (May 2026; ~$70bn basic market cap on day one) is the defining realized-able position, since an IPO is a liquidity event but distribution depends on lock-up and selling. Earlier exits were mostly modest M&A (6 River Systems to Shopify, $450m, 2019; Kindred to Ocado, 2020; ClearMetal to project44, 2021). Lucira Health (IPO 2021) went bankrupt in 2023.
firms.recent_activity: Led Redwood's $350m Series E (Oct 2025) and Mind Robotics' $115m seed, co-led Bedrock Robotics and Genesis AI, and backed Oxide, Mytra ($120m C), SkyRyse ($300m C), Cellares ($257m D) and AheadComputing in 2025-26. It is building more companies in-house under the 'physical AI' thesis.
firms.watch_items: AUM has scaled to ~$10bn with larger median checks, so the firm is moving toward growth-stage pricing. Concentration in Cerebras, which faces customer-concentration questions (G42/UAE), makes distribution discipline after lock-up a key LP item.

He invests without an investment committee across seed through growth, often writing large late-stage checks. His early bets include Airbnb, Stripe, Coinbase, Square, Instacart, Figma, Notion, Anduril and Rippling, and his AI-era bets include Perplexity, Harvey, Mistral and Character.ai. Fund sizes rose from $620M (2021) to $1B+ (2024, third fund). The Information reported in mid-2025 that he was raising ~$1.5B, possibly toward $2-3B; the final close is unconfirmed.

Fund II closed May-2025 at US$200m with Hyundai Motor and Kia as anchor investors. Third-party databases list check sizes of US$10-200m.

firms.name: Founders Fund
firms.overview: Peter Thiel, Ken Howery and Luke Nosek founded the firm in 2005. Anduril (co-founded by partner Trae Stephens) and SpaceX dominate NAV. The firm runs a small early-stage vehicle (FF VIII, cut to ~$0.9bn, with a further ~$0.9bn early fund in Oct 2025) and much larger growth funds. Growth III closed at $4.6bn (2025) and Growth IV at ~$6bn (2026, ~$1.5bn of it from partners), its fastest succession ever.

firms.name: Radical Ventures
firms.overview: Jordan Jacobs and Tomi Poutanen, co-founders of Layer 6 AI and the Vector Institute, founded Radical in 2017. It invests only in AI companies, from formation through growth. Main markup driver: Cohere ($20.5bn Series E first close, Oct 2026). firms.name: Sequoia Capital (US/Europe)
firms.overview: Don Valentine founded Sequoia in 1972. It is the archetypal multi-stage venture firm, with early stakes in Apple, Cisco, Google, Nvidia, WhatsApp, Stripe and Airbnb. In 2021 the US/Europe business moved to an open-ended evergreen structure: LPs invest in The Sequoia Capital Fund, which feeds closed-end sub-funds (Arc/seed, venture, growth, expansion). The evergreen fund was reported at $13.6bn in early 2023 and close to $20bn by 2025, and the firm is a registered investment adviser. Sequoia split from HongShan (China) and Peak XV (India/SEA) in 2023-24. In Nov 2025 Roelof Botha stepped down as senior steward and Alfred Lin and Pat Grady became co-stewards. Their first major raise was a ~$7bn expansion fund (Apr 2026) for late-stage AI positions such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
firms.performance: Sequoia publishes no fund-level returns. Washington State Investment Board (as of 2025-09-30) reports Sequoia Global Growth Fund III - Endurance Partners (initial investment Jun 2018, $350m commitment) at 16.16% net IRR, 2.0x TVPI and ~0.47x DPI (calculated). Newcomer's UTIMCO analysis (Jan 2025) says Sequoia's 2020 and 2021 funds were outperforming most peers but gives no figures. Botha oversaw ~$50bn of distributions to LPs during his tenure (2022-25). FTX was written to zero (~$214m loss).
firms.recent_activity: Reported pace is ~126 new investments in 2025 and ~66 in H1 2026 (third-party count), with roughly 60% of new capital going to AI. 2026 deals include co-leading Anthropic's ~$965bn Series H (May 2026) and leading ElevenLabs' Series D ($11bn, Feb 2026). Sequoia is also in xAI (now inside SpaceX), SSI, OpenEvidence, Harvey and Kalshi.
firms.watch_items: The post-Botha leadership transition and the move to concentrated expansion-stage AI bets both change the firm's risk profile. Evergreen liquidity terms and the absence of public fund-level reporting make it harder for LPs to benchmark.

firms.name: Tiger Global Management
firms.overview: Chase Coleman founded Tiger Global in 2001 as a Tiger Management spin-out. Its Private Investment Partners (PIP) funds started in 2003 under Scott Shleifer and became known for early China and India internet bets (JD.com, Flipkart). In 2021-22 the firm scaled up sharply: it backed 300+ startups in 2021 and raised PIP 15 at $12.7bn, at the time the largest venture fund ever, deploying most of it at peak prices. In 2022 the hedge fund fell about 56% and the private book was marked down about a third. Since then Tiger has reset. Shleifer moved to an advisory role in Nov 2023, PIP 16 closed at $2.2bn (target was $6bn), and PIP 17 (about $2-2.2bn target, first close Mar 2026) returns to a concentrated, AI-led book anchored by the Tiger team.

firms.overview: Lip-Bu Tan (founder of Walden International, ex-CEO of Cadence, Intel CEO since March 2025) and Young Sohn (ex-President and CSO of Samsung Electronics) formed Walden Catalyst in 2020. It invests in early-stage data and AI, semiconductors, cloud infrastructure, robotics and bio-x-tech companies across the US, Europe and Israel. Its inaugural fund closed above $550m in November 2021 against a $400m target. In 2025 the portfolio saw Rivos acquired by Meta and new rounds at Empower Semiconductor ($140m+ Series D), ANYbotics ($127m) and Amperesand ($80m Series A, co-led with Temasek). The WCV site lists Habana, Nuvia, SambaNova, IonQ, Graphcore, Inphi and Zoom as 'past investments', which reflect partners' and Walden International's legacy track record.
firms.check_size: Seed to Series B; leads and co-leads up to ~$15-20m (e.g., Clarity, Amperesand)
firms.performance: Not publicly disclosed. Fund I realized Rivos (acquired by Meta, announced 2025; price undisclosed). Most Fund I marks are unrealized. The partners' historical track record (Habana to Intel, Nuvia to Qualcomm, Inphi to Marvell, Mellanox to Nvidia, Zoom) comes from prior vehicles and should not be attributed to WCV Fund I.
firms.recent_activity: 2025 rounds include Empower Semiconductor's $140m+ Series D, ANYbotics' $127m, Amperesand's $80m Series A (co-lead), Virtue AI's $30m seed/A and ATI Motors' $20m Series B. Newer AI infra names include Hyperbolic, RadixArk and Neocognition.
firms.watch_items: Key-person risk is significant: Lip-Bu Tan has been Intel CEO since March 2025, which raises time-allocation and conflict questions (e.g., SambaNova, where Tan has been chairman and Intel reportedly explored an acquisition). No successor fund had been confirmed in sources reviewed.
